correctness.rationale: Case split by initial hub color shows rim time-two excitation exactly for a length-five motif when hub=1, and hub time-two excitation exactly for two distinct 101 motifs when hub=q-1. Other hub colors have no time-two activity. In each channel, incompatible support motifs or missing rim contacts exclude all time-three excitation. This proves the universal extinction bound \(q+1\), and explicit rim words prove sharpness (q for \(n=3\)). The de Bruijn trace is a bijection to cyclic words; independent exhaustive simulation and weighted transfer counts match for tested n,q. No finite experiment is used to justify an infinite claim.

value.rationale: For the natural all-size wheel graph family, the exact maximal-life shell is controlled by two local microscopic transmission mechanisms, with a computable finite transfer formula for each q,n and a positive asymptotic probability \(2/q\). This simultaneously identifies a sharp change from the three-state wheel clock and a robust macroscopic population of maximal transients, rather than a routine fixed-size enumeration.
